study.question: After cycling positive auxiliary labels retained most of the external-orientation AUC gap, can per-task batch prevalence replace example-specific labels in the positive-label-only orientation source while retaining that gap under the frozen strongest joint-model lineage?
study.hypothesis: The sign preference from the positive-label-only orientation source may primarily reflect marginal auxiliary prevalence interacting with recipient Jacobians rather than correct per-example auxiliary label assignment. Replacing source labels by their per-task batch means may retain most of the positive-minus-negative orientation gap. This hypothesis concerns only the orientation-bit source: it does not assert that useful auxiliary supervision can be removed from private learning or from native transfer geometry. It remains unverified.

nearest_work.difference: Read the standalone native positive-label bridge and all training-loss/collection/reduction paths. Retain BCE(y_source)-BCE(0), seven identity collection edges, detached source VJPs and unchanged native geometry. Add only per-task batch-mean source targets and an equal-work mean BCE graph; cross source assignment with external orientation.

Authorized receipt/config inspected: prior mean-label source used full BCE(mean labels), retaining its prediction-dependent term. This proposal applies mean labels to BCE(mean)-BCE(0), isolating the positive-label contribution. It is not a duplicate mean-full-source experiment; no ancestor source for round67 is available here.

Archived exact-version primary text (content-sha256:5fee25f33f375e51b3ee9417d376ff9dbe2ea3628c932a7679ddfeb0feaaade2), lines56-120, supports target-conditioned local activation inherited through the joint model. This study leaves that architecture fixed and studies a training-only surrogate; it is not an exact DIN reproduction or a new attention architecture.

Pinned benchmark source (git:90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d), forward lines123-170 inspected: task-mask sequence hubs, categorical/task tokens and stacked interaction. Adding these forward mechanisms would confound the current source-label question. No hub architecture is adopted. The original INFNet paper has only link/provenance available in the registry, so original-paper equivalence, priority and exhaustive novelty remain unverified.

inherited_components: All model representations, compression, field matching, moment summaries, action information, prediction heads and rank-16 product context/history interactions from the accepted joint-model lineage.

study.proposed_difference: Observation: DIN AUC0.6555440824, joint replay0.6684573079 and click-only/aux-context-blocked0.6678548721 established the initial shared-gradient question; rolled auxiliary labels0.6674639466 were harmful. Later fixed-angle canonical-bit removal produced near-equal orientations (positive0.6687682992, negative0.6687531803). Full BCE(mean-label) sources likewise had a small gap (positive0.6686740459, negative0.6686874913). In contrast, round72 native positive-label bridges yielded positive0.6688260412608873 versus negative0.6682300757043065 (gap0.0005959655565808), while cycling labels yielded positive0.6687278997261598 versus negative0.6681462383750754 (gap0.0005816613510844). The assignment-by-orientation interaction was only0.0000143042054964; native-minus-cycle differences were0.0000981415347275 and0.0000838373292311. Zero-target-only source gaps were also small (round70 positive0.6685638449, negative0.6686228172). These positive, null and unsuccessful directions justify removing remaining label-assignment variability in the positive-only source. Implement detached FP32 per-task means over every training row, broadcast to recipients, and differentiate BCE(mean)-BCE(0) only for the source orientation bit. All cells execute native/cycle/mean/zero source graphs; native bridges isolate the added graph work. No new result is measured here. Public code and accepted receipts are available; raw data/checkpoints/GPU and torch are not available for rechecking digests or reproducing tensor runs in this phase. Preserve the accepted protocol/source/data hashes without claiming a fresh readiness pass. No previous_runtime_error is reported. No human-owned knowledge is modified; agent-memory search yielded no scoped records, so the observations and limitations are recorded prospectively here for the host receipt/archive, not written to an invented memory store.
predictions: Validity first: corresponding native bridges should reproduce the round72 positive0.6688260412608873 and negative0.6682300757043065 AUC within absolute1e-6. A failed bridge prevents interpreting the new comparison as isolated.

Define D_native=AUC(native,positive)-AUC(native,negative), D_mean analogously, and interaction I=D_native-D_mean. If marginal prevalence supports most of the orientation behavior, D_mean should remain positive and at least0.5*D_native; report all four AUCs and I. This is a predeclared descriptive discrimination threshold, not a significance/equivalence test.

At a fixed batch/state, replacing source targets changes only the selected source cotangents/one-bit summary: forward probabilities, real scalar joint BCE value, direct private parameter gradients and true-label native transfer line/radius/gates remain identical. Training-only labels never enter inference.

Expected learned capacity remains32192421, with identical inference work. The additional mean source losses/VJP traversal add training cost; measure allocated GPU seconds, wall/train seconds, examples, peak memory and inference throughput/p50/p95 instead of claiming equal compute.
All four task AUC/Logloss values, auxiliary mean AUC and existing history slices with sample/positive/negative counts remain secondary. No new bins or held-out feedback are used.
falsifiers: With successful bridges, a nonpositive D_mean or a contraction to at most0.25*D_native opposes marginal prevalence retaining the observed orientation behavior. Ratios between0.25 and0.5 remain ambiguous. A lack of measured bit perturbation/active support prevents treating a null as a mechanism refutation.

If mean-source outcomes track the existing canonical-bit-removal trajectories and a host fixed-state probe reveals a constant/fallback source bit, reject a label-prevalence explanation in favor of a degenerate or generic orientation control; do not count this as informative auxiliary supervision.

If a bridge misses its tolerance, private gradients change directly, source labels reach inference, capacity changes, or transfer radius/gates change at a fixed state, invalidate attribution and diagnose without changing the frozen contract.

A single-seed gain without paired seed repetition, or a gain reproduced by replacement/degenerate controls, does not establish a supervision mechanism. A failure of this source replacement does not refute all auxiliary supervision.
alternative_explanations: This is a shared-context row-space surrogate VJP; its geometry is not parameter-space orthogonality after embedding scatter/optimizers.
Batch means remove individual assignments, sparsity and joint label tuples together; source magnitude changes before a one-bit reduction although actual transfer radius is native at a fixed state.
True auxiliary labels remain in private training and native transfer geometry; recipient probabilities, Dice batch coupling and earlier states remain informative.

Zero or numerically degenerate source tangents default to +1. The documented host does not automatically collect source_bit_diagnostics; without a fixed-state bit-disagreement/degeneracy probe, performance alone leaves orientation attribution provisional.
Training trajectories diverge after intervention; fixed-state invariants are not claims of equal geometry across separately trained final models.
One frozen training seed and repeated adaptive validation selection cannot establish population significance or independent repeated support.
